references.text: The Lord commanded Moses to prepare the people for the third day, when He would come down on Mount Sinai. The same command regarding preparation for the morning is repeated here.
The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses up to Him, parallel to the command here to stand at the top of the mountain.
Moses had previously been called up the mountain to receive the stone tablets. Now he is called up again after the first tablets were broken.
Israel camped before Mount Sinai, which is the same mountain Moses is now commanded to go up.
The fulfillment of the command in verse 2: Moses rose early in the morning and went up on Mount Sinai as the Lord had commanded.
Moses recounts how the Lord told him to carve two new stone tablets and go up the mountain, a parallel account of this event.
Psalm 43 interprets the story of Mount Sinai as a symbol of the soul's longing for God's presence and truth.
Nehemiah confirms and summarizes the event at Mount Sinai that Moses was instructed to prepare for in Exodus.
